b3a20e920c039baa.description: Company Description Zenlynx Technology is an AI-powered Enterprise Sustainability and Climate Intelligence company that helps organizations turn complex sustainability, ESG, climate, energy, and operational data into actionable business insights. Its flagship platform, ZenX, unifies fragmented enterprise data, automates sustainability workflows, and delivers real-time performance, risk, and compliance intelligence. ZenX combines Artificial Intelligence, data integration, analytics, automation, and domain expertise to simplify ESG reporting, climate disclosures, sustainability management, carbon accounting, and energy intelligence. The companys mission is to make sustainability a strategic business advantage rather than a reporting burden, enabling transparency, resilience, operational excellence, and long-term value creation. Zenlynx works with modern enterprises that seek to accelerate sustainable growth through intelligent technology. Role Description The Software Engineer Intern role is a remote internship position focused on supporting the development and enhancement of Zenlynxs AI-driven sustainability platform. The intern will collaborate with engineering teams to design, implement, test, and maintain back-end services and APIs that power data integration, analytics, and workflow automation. Day-to-day tasks may include writing clean and efficient code, debugging and resolving issues, participating in code reviews, and contributing to technical documentation. The role also involves learning and applying best practices in software development, working with modern tools and frameworks, and supporting the delivery of reliable and scalable features for enterprise customers. The intern will be expected to work closely with mentors, proactively seek feedback, and continuously build technical and problem-solving skills. Qualifications Strong foundational knowledge in Computer Science, including data structures, algorithms, and software engineering principles.Skills in Software Development and Programming, with experience in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, Java, JavaScript, or similar).Understanding of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts and ability to apply them in designing and implementing maintainable code.Exposure to Back-End Web Development, such as building APIs, working with databases, or using server-side frameworks.Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field.Ability to learn quickly, work independently in a remote environment, and collaborate effectively within a distributed team.Familiarity with version control (e.g., Git) and basic software development workflows; experience with cloud platforms or AI/ML tools is a plus.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and interest in sustainability, ESG, or climate technology. .

b395486b886308ce.description: Location: Bangalore & Gurgaon - Hybrid (India) Employment Type: Full-Time About Us We are actively building the next generation of intelligent product ecosystems. Our team doesn't just talk about artificial intelligencewe deploy production-grade LLM pipelines, vector search workflows, and scalable AI infrastructure into real-world applications every single week. If you are passionate about generative AI, low-latency inference, and turning cutting-edge research into reliable software, you will find your home here. The Role We are seeking an innovative AI / Machine Learning Engineer to take charge of our AI infrastructure. You will design, fine-tune, and scale artificial intelligence systems, integrating advanced LLM providers and vector databases into our core product architecture. You will work closely with our core engineering team to ensure our AI features are fast, cost-effective, and deeply integrated. Key Responsibilities RAG Implementation: Architect and scale Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) frameworks using vector databases like Qdrant or Pinecone. LLM & Prompt Optimization: Optimize prompt engineering workflows, manage token limits, and evaluate performance across various LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, open-source models). Inference Engineering: Build and maintain low-latency, scalable AI inference endpoints using Python and FastAPI. Model Fine-Tuning: Fine-tune open-source models on domain-specific datasets to improve accuracy and business relevance. Pipeline Monitoring: Monitor AI system accuracy, latency, and cost efficiency, implementing caching strategies and fallback mechanisms. What We Are Looking For (Requirements) Experience: 3+ years of professional software/ML engineering experience with a strong focus on production-grade AI systems. Python Mastery: Deep expertise in Python, asynchronous programming, and modern frameworks like FastAPI. Vector & Database Skills: Hands-on experience with vector databases (Qdrant, Pinecone) and relational databases (MySQL/PostgreSQL). LLM Ecosystem Knowledge: Proven experience working with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Hugging Face transformers, and major LLM APIs. System Thinking: Strong grasp of API design, Docker containerization, and cloud deployment (AWS/GCP). What We Offer Competitive Compensation: Top-tier salary bracket paired with performance bonuses and equity options. Cutting-Edge Stack: Freedom to experiment with and deploy the latest AI models and frameworks. Learning & Development: Dedicated stipend for AI conferences, research papers, and advanced certifications. Flexibility &Wellness: Remote-first culture and comprehensive health insurance for you and your family. Our Hiring Process Initial Screening: 30-minute introductory chat with our recruitment team. Technical Assessment: Practical take-home coding challenge or LLM integration task. Deep Dive & System Design: Architecture discussion focused on RAG pipelines, scaling, and past ML projects. b323a085150dc27e.description: This role gets AI into production and keeps it running. You own the MLOps backbone and build the agentic systems we deliver for clients: agents, GraphRAG, enterprise copilots, and workflow automation. The particular challenge here is dependability. An LLM system that dazzles in a demo can behave unpredictably in a client's real workflow, and your job is to make it steady: reliable, affordable to run, guarded, and watched. That's the problem this role turns over, and if it's the kind of problem you enjoy, there's plenty of it. **The work:** * Design and ship agentic systems: agents, RAG and GraphRAG, copilots the client's people actually use * Own the model-specific side of production: serving logic, evaluation, guardrails, drift and behavior monitoring, and the retraining loop * Build the MLOps frameworks and reusable AI infrastructure every engagement draws on * Expose models and agents behind clean endpoints for the applications to consume * Integrate AI into the client's real operational workflows, not tools that sit unused **Where your work ends.** You take models from the Data Scientist and the graph foundation from the Data Engineer and turn them into dependable production AI. You own everything model-specific, but you run it on the platform the Software Engineer provides: you don't own the containers, Kubernetes, cloud provisioning, or the generic observability stack, and you don't build the application front ends. Your line is model behavior; theirs is the platform and the product surface. **What success looks like:** * AI systems stay reliable in a client's real workflow, not just in a demo * Guardrails, evals, and monitoring are in place before anything goes live * The cost of running AI stays predictable and defensible * The AI infrastructure you build makes the next engagement faster, not slower The stack we work in today: Python for the model and service work, with FastAPI where you're exposing a model or agent behind an endpoint; PyTorch, with real fluency in LLM internals, fine-tuning, and, where it earns its place, mechanistic interpretability; MCP and A2A for agent and tool interop; and Neo4j behind our GraphRAG systems. A depth in a serious slice of this, plus the judgment to learn the rest, matters more than checking every box. For this role, MLOps is the craft itself. **About The Strong AI, and how we work** The Strong AI is an end-to-end AI implementation partner. Clients come to us because most organizations can run an AI experiment, but few can turn it into a system their business depends on. We close that gap. We don't hand over slideware or a notebook; we build systems that work inside a client's business, and where they want it, we run them. You'll work across engagements and industries, on different problems and often different stacks. We're technology-agnostic: the problem and the client's environment choose the tools, so treat any stack we list as the ground we work on today, not a gate. **Across all roles, we ask for the same way of working:** * Real software. Tested, reviewed, versioned code the next person, or the client's team, can pick up. * MLOps mindset. A model's life starts at deployment. Monitoring, retraining, drift, and rollback are handled before anything breaks. * Systems thinking. You see both the value slice and the whole it compounds into. * Quality and security, owned by you. Designed in from the first decision, not inspected in at the end. Everyone builds to the highest standard. * Built for handover. Clear code and docs the client's own team can understand, operate, and take over.

b3fed030a3851a69.description: Associate Product Manager/ Product Manager Supply Chain Team: Product | Location: Mumbai (Work from Office) About the Team Purplle's Product Management team builds the technology products that power a comprehensive e-commerce platform. The team constantly ships new supply chain features that are scalable, reduce cost, and enhance customer experience. As a lean team, every individual is expected to make a significant, measurable impact on the business. About the Role We are looking for an Associate Product Manager who will own our Warehouse Management System (WMS) and internal supply chain tools as the core of the role, while also driving our ERP integration and our data platforms for reporting and data warehousing. You will work at the intersection of product, operations, and data, turning the needs of warehouse stakeholders into reliable, well-built features. This is an individual contributor role that works closely with the data engineering, backend engineering, and analytics teams, as well as operations and business stakeholders, to deliver the roadmap. Key Responsibilities Warehouse Management and Internal Tools Own the product roadmap for the WMS and adjacent internal tools used by warehouse teams. Translate operational problems into clear Product Requirement Documents, use cases, and acceptance criteria for engineering and QA. Partner with backend engineering to design, build, and roll out new features, and drive adoption with operations teams. Identify workflow gaps and inefficiencies on the ground, then define structured improvements that scale. ERP Systems Support the integration and data consistency between the WMS and the ERP for sales, inventory, and reconciliation flows. Work with engineering and operations to debug system-level discrepancies and drive root causes to closure. Help define and validate the impact of ERP-related product changes. Data Platforms, Reporting, and Data Warehousing Lead the reporting and data warehousing layer that gives stakeholders a single, reliable source of truth. Coordinate with the data engineering team on ETL processes and pipelines that feed the warehouse. Build and maintain dashboards and reports covering inventory positions, stock movements, reconciliation health, and system performance. Use data analysis to surface insights and drive data-informed product decisions. Must-Have Skills and Requirements 1+ years of experience in a product, analytics, or supply-chain technology role. BE / B.Tech from a reputed institute. MBA is a plus but not mandatory. Working knowledge of SQL and comfort querying datasets in a cloud warehouse such as BigQuery. Solid data analysis fundamentals and the ability to understand discrepancies across systems. Familiarity with ETL processes and pipelines and how data moves from source systems into a data warehouse. Ability to write clear PRDs and use cases, and to think and work in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities. Strong verbal and written communication and stakeholder management skills across product, engineering, and business teams. High ownership mindset with the ability to drive a problem from identification to resolution. Good-to-Have Skills Exposure to Warehouse Management Systems and ERP systems, and an understanding of how inventory and sales data flow between them. Hands-on experience with BI or data visualization tools such as Looker, Tableau, or Metabase. Experience with SAP or a similar enterprise ERP. Exposure to inventory management, or quick-commerce and dark-store operations. Familiarity with pipeline orchestration tools such as Airflow. What You Will Gain End-to-end ownership of the WMS and internal tools that run day-to-day supply chain operations. A role at the intersection of product, supply chain, and technology, with real influence on the roadmap. Deep exposure to ERP integration and to building the data platform behind business-critical reporting. A clear growth path from Associate Product Manager toward a full Product Manager role. .
